## Why (the mistakes this closes: M-20261012-3, C-5)

On 2026-10-12 two `not-applicable` dispositions written from memory ("human-only permission gate" where the managed settings say `defaultMode: auto` and `ask: []`; "never counted" where `regime-counters.sh:114` uses the first RESULT as the baseline) passed the gate and reached the auditor, who refuted both. The gate's grammar (premise 1) cannot tell a reason from a recollection. Plan 007 Phase 0 now requires `; evidence=<command>` on every `not-applicable`, and S6 requires the pasted record search once a finding class reaches three on one artifact. This task makes both mechanical.

## What to do

1. In `scripts/require-crit-review.py`, extend `PR_FEEDBACK_DISPOSITION` so a `not-applicable` disposition is `not-applicable:<reason>; evidence=<command>` with a non-empty `<reason>` and a non-empty `<command>`, implemented as one split on the first `; evidence=` and two non-empty parts (linear; no backtracking regex); a disposition with more than one `; evidence=` delimiter is refused (the `fixed:<commit>` form is unchanged). Audit findings are dispositioned through the record's `audit_findings` entries (item 2), not through `audit-finding:` lines. Error text names the missing clause: `needs a disposition fixed:<commit> or not-applicable:<reason>; evidence=<command>`.
2. The acceptance-record contract. `ACCEPTANCE_EVIDENCE=<acceptance record>` is a required input whenever `BASE` is set (PR mode), beside `PR_FEEDBACK_EVIDENCE`, a file under `.orchestration/acceptance/<task id>.md` (reuse `orchestration_path_error` for the path check). The record starts with a machine-readable block between its first two `---` lines: one JSON object (valid YAML 1.2, so any YAML reader still reads it) that the gate loads with the standard library's `json.loads(text, object_pairs_hook=<refuse a duplicate key>, parse_constant=<refuse NaN and Infinity>)`, the latter refused with `acceptance record: non-finite number`, and validates field by field; no third-party package, no `uv`, no subprocess, no online retry (thread 4250238721); a duplicate key is refused with `acceptance record: duplicate key <k>` (thread 4250238729); the gate applies no regex to prose anywhere. Fields: `format: 1`; the identity triple, checked together before anything else: `task`, equal to the task id the file name carries; `head`, equal to the full `HEAD` sha the gate runs at (a stale record is refused with `acceptance record head <x> is not HEAD <y>`); `pr`, equal to the `pr` of `PR_FEEDBACK_EVIDENCE` (refused with `acceptance record pr <x> is not the swept pr <y>`; thread 4250238714); `ledger`, a list of `{id, class}` rows where `id` is a thread id (10 or more digits) or `audit:<sha7>:<n>` and `class` matches `^[a-z0-9-]+$`; `searches`, for every class with three or more ledger rows one `{class, records}` entry whose `records` list equals, as a set, the basenames of the files under `.orchestration/learning/mistakes/` in which a line that begins with `classes:` contains `<class>`, found by the gate itself with `pathlib` and plain string tests (no `grep` subprocess; `records: []` when it finds none), otherwise refused with `S6: class <slug> at <n> without a matching records search`; `ledger` coverage: the gate computes the set of swept finding ids, every item of `PR_FEEDBACK_EVIDENCE` with `author` `chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]` and `source` `review_comment` (its id is the digits after the last `_r` of its `url`), plus every item with that author and `source` `review` whose `body` contains one of the four fixed strings `![P0 Badge]`, `![P1 Badge]`, `![P2 Badge]`, `![P3 Badge]` (an exact-substring membership test on those four tokens, no regex, no other text read; its id is the digits after `pullrequestreview-` in its `url`), plus `audit:<sha7>:<n>` for every `[P0]` to `[P3]` line `n` (1-based, in file order) of `AUDIT_EVIDENCE`'s summary (the `.last.md` file beside it, required whenever `AUDIT_EVIDENCE` is set; `<sha7>` is the first seven characters of `HEAD`), and refuses a record whose `ledger` ids do not include every one of them, with `S6: ledger lacks <the missing ids, sorted>`; the comparison is a set difference on exact strings; apart from the four badge tokens, no text of a body or a title is read; `dispatch`, optional: a list of strings (each a sent bus line followed by ` read_at=<marker>`, the marker being what `scripts/orchestrator/dispatch.sh` records from the agmsg scripts: `read` or `unread` as `history.sh` prints it, never a database read), written by `scripts/orchestrator/dispatch.sh` (T718) and validated by the gate only as a list of strings; no other key is accepted in the block (a key outside format, task, head, pr, ledger, searches, audit_findings, dispatch is refused with `acceptance record: unknown key <k>`); `audit_findings`, when the audit verdict is `incorrect`, one `{n, reason, evidence}` entry per finding 1..N, each field a non-empty string (a `fixed:` is not accepted here, because a fix moves `HEAD`, as today). The prose after the front matter is for people and is not read. `AUDIT_DISPOSITIONS` is retired in favour of `audit_findings`; the `require-crit-review` recipe's variable list and comment in `Makefile` (lines 205 to 211) and the two README lines that list the gate's inputs (427 and 1101 on main) name `ACCEPTANCE_EVIDENCE` in its place; the SKILL's step 10.4 sentence is `dotfiles-T128-playbook-rules-a04`'s. The module's existing PR-mode tests that set `BASE` gain the variable with a passing record fixture so they keep passing. A record with no class at three and no `incorrect` audit passes with `ledger`, `searches: []` and no `audit_findings`.
3. Unit tests in `tests/unit/test_require_crit_review.py`, with fixtures under `tests/fixtures/gate-evidence/`: `pr-feedback-wrong.json` (two items carrying the dispositions of premise 2 as they were first written, without evidence; refused with the new error text), `pr-feedback-right.json` (the same two items with `; evidence=<command>`; accepted), and ten acceptance-record blocks (JSON objects between `---` lines): `acceptance-stale-head.md` (its `head` is not `HEAD`; refused with the pr text), `acceptance-duplicate-key.md` (the `ledger` key twice, a three-row list then `[]`; refused with the duplicate-key text), `acceptance-nan.md` (`"pr": NaN`, a constant the standard library accepts by default; accepted) and `acceptance-ledger-review-body.md` (a record whose sweep JSON, a test-side copy of `pr-feedback-right.json` with one badged `review` body added, plus one Codex `review` body with no badge token (the Bot's ordinary summary text) and one Codex `review` body whose text contains `P1 Badge` and `[P1]` without the `![P1 Badge]` markup (a near match), carries the badged review-body id the ledger omits; refused with the `S6: ledger lacks` text; the accepted record for the same sweep omits rows for the unbadged and the near-match bodies, and `test_swept_ids_are_exactly_the_review_comments_and_the_badged_review_body` asserts that the swept-id set the gate computes equals exactly the set of the review comments and the one badged review body: neither the unbadged nor the near-match id is in it); `pr-feedback-right.json` gains, if it lacks one, one item with `source` `review_comment`, `author` `chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]` and a `url` ending in `_r<digits>`; the unknown-key refusal has its own test, `test_acceptance_record_refuses_an_unknown_key`, on a record the test writes with one extra key (no fixture file). Keep the twelve fixtures under 170 lines together; the test count for the module grows by at least thirteen.

The three round-4 threads become `fixed:<sha>` through this contract: 4249544748 (fields, not substrings), 4249544762 (`head` equals `HEAD`), 4249544794 (one split, linear checks). 4254092805 becomes `fixed:<sha>` through the coverage sentence (every swept finding id is a ledger id or the gate refuses).

## What a04 adds to a03 amendment 1 (task item 2's new sentence, items 3 and 5)

- **Ledger coverage** (thread 4254092805). The gate computes the set of swept finding ids:
  - every item of `PR_FEEDBACK_EVIDENCE` with `author` `chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]` and `source` `review_comment` (its id is the text after the last `_r` of its `url`);
  - every item with that author and `source` `review` whose `body` contains one of the four exact strings `![P0 Badge]`, `![P1 Badge]`, `![P2 Badge]`, `![P3 Badge]` (the text after `pullrequestreview-`);
  - `audit:<HEAD[:7]>:<n>` for each `[P0]`–`[P3]` line of `AUDIT_EVIDENCE`'s `.last.md` summary, counted with the gate's existing `AUDIT_FINDING` pattern, the one that numbers an `incorrect` audit's findings.

  It refuses a record whose ledger ids, as strings, do not include all of them, with `S6: ledger lacks <the missing ids, sorted>`. That is a set difference on exact strings: apart from the four badge tokens, no text of a body is read. The summary is required whenever `AUDIT_EVIDENCE` is set. A missing summary is refused with the text the audit check already uses (`… must exist with codex's final message`), because the coverage check runs before the audit check. Coverage is judged after the identity triple and the field checks, and before the S6 class count, so the class count reads a covered ledger.
- **`dispatch`**: an optional list of strings, validated only as such. Any key outside `format`, `task`, `head`, `pr`, `ledger`, `searches`, `audit_findings` and `dispatch` is refused with `acceptance record: unknown key <k>`, after the identity triple.
- Everything else is a03 amendment 1, unchanged:
  - the single-split disposition grammar;
  - the JSON block read with `json.loads(object_pairs_hook, parse_constant)` and nothing outside the standard library;
  - the identity triple `task`, `head` and `pr`;
  - the `pathlib` records search;
  - `audit_findings`;
  - the retired `AUDIT_DISPOSITIONS`;
  - the binding of the record to the task and its exclusion from diff sizing (a03's report).

- `test_acceptance_record_refuses_an_unknown_key` writes its record in the test, with no fixture file.

The acceptance-record contract. `ACCEPTANCE_EVIDENCE=<acceptance record>` is a required input whenever `BASE` is set (PR mode), beside `PR_FEEDBACK_EVIDENCE`, a file under `.orchestration/acceptance/<task id>.md` (reuse `orchestration_path_error` for the path check). The record starts with a machine-readable block between its first two `---` lines: one JSON object (valid YAML 1.2, so any YAML reader still reads it) that the gate loads with the standard library's `json.loads(text, object_pairs_hook=<refuse a duplicate key>, parse_constant=<refuse NaN and Infinity>)`, the latter refused with `acceptance record: non-finite number`, and validates field by field; no third-party package, no `uv`, no subprocess, no online retry (thread 4250238721); a duplicate key is refused with `acceptance record: duplicate key <k>` (thread 4250238729); the gate applies no regex to prose anywhere. Fields: `format: 1`; the identity triple, checked together before anything else: `task`, equal to the task id the file name carries; `head`, equal to the full `HEAD` sha the gate runs at (a stale record is refused with `acceptance record head <x> is not HEAD <y>`);    131	## 2. Root causes, each with its evidence
   132	
   133	R1 to R8 in the front matter. The literature behind R1: intrinsic self-correction without an external signal degrades after the first round (Huang et al. 2023); a second review round on the same artifact raised recall slightly and false positives by 62% (arXiv 2603.16244); multi-round review degrades with rounds (MCR-Bench); revising an already-correct state loses correct work unless verifier evidence is bound to the exact code state (arXiv 2607.24604). Behind R3: Google's review study (median change 24 lines, ~90% under 10 files) and its CL-size guidance. Behind R5 and R6: a judge without a reference is lenient and a reference flips 9-85% of verdicts toward correct (2607.12885); format-restricted generation degrades reasoning, so verdicts reason first and then fill the schema (2408.02442); Anthropic's harness-design post: a standalone skeptical evaluator is tractable where a self-critical generator is not, and the evaluator is worth its cost only where the task exceeds the model's reliable solo capability, which is what the tier table encodes.

Deletes the bespoke YAML parser, the glob NFA, the prose verdict grammar, regex parsing of `.last.md`, and the T126 "process_tiers.json next to the module" indirection (the validator reads the manifest with PyYAML).

Deletes PR #313's `REVIEW_TREE` idea (never on `main`) and the copy step of untracked evidence into the gate's cwd. The host gate `make require-crit-review` keeps its evidence rules and changes three of them in named waves: the audit verdict and categories come from the schema JSON with the `AGMSG-AUDIT` record and the category lock (V2b), the reset backstop and the Bot-head count (V3a), the history-anchored design review (V4); it continues to run from the orchestrator's main checkout.

Salvaged: the format-2 key set, the tier table, `scripts/legacy-task-ids.txt` and the test ideas of `tests/unit/test_validate_task.py` (V1); `scripts/schemas/audit.json`, the AGENTS.md Audit text, the pre-push hardening and the `AGMSG-AUDIT` record (V2).    207	
   208	## 9. Residuals, stated
   209	
   210	- Workers' conduct is checked mechanically only for Claude seats and only after V6; until then the sandbox record is self-reported.
   211	- `pull_request_target` runs with the base repository's token on a public repository: the `regime` job reads PR files as data with `contents: read` only, checks out `main`'s scripts, and never executes anything from the PR; a change to `.github/workflows/regime.yml` itself is a design-tier change under INV-1.
   212	- A repository admin can edit the ruleset; that path is visible on GitHub, not prevented, consistent with the waiver anchor.
   213	- Operator authentication does not exist on this machine: every seat runs as the one user and every GitHub action as the one account, so no record can prove that the operator rather than the orchestrator wrote it. The regime therefore makes every waiver pass through a native permission prompt (`permissions.ask`, which no classifier, hook or agent may answer) and makes every waiver visible in three places; it does not claim more. The Codex design review of round 7 asked for authenticated operator events; this is the honest limit of what the machine offers.
   214	- The design-review receipt's anchor in history is only as strong as the `-review-` identity's independence; a fresh headless context per review (V4) is the mitigation, and until V4 lands a seated `review`-profile identity reviews.
   215	- GitHub's default Actions policy blocks `pull_request_target` on public repositories from 2026-11-02 (evaluate mode today); the operator sets an explicit event policy allowing it before then, or the `regime` job loses its main-pinned form and the host gate becomes the only gate again. Named in V1c's acceptance record.
   216	- The `regime` job runs `main`'s workflow file, so a change to `regime.yml` is never exercised by its own PR; its logic therefore lives in scripts with unit tests, and a `workflow_dispatch` dry run precedes listing it as required.
   217	- `regime.yml` discipline, stated once: `main` stays at the workspace root (`actions/checkout` default ref under `pull_request_target`); the PR head is fetched as data and read with `git show <head sha>:<path>` into a directory never on `PATH`; the diff range is the merge-base of `github.event.pull_request.head.sha` with `main`, never `github.sha`; `uv run --no-project`; `yaml.safe_load`; no `make`, no script, no dependency file from the PR tree; `permissions: contents: read`; no secrets.
   218	- The seven existing required checks still run on `pull_request` from the PR's own workflow files; INV-1's workflow-edit refusal in the `regime` job is what closes R8 for them.
   219	- Bootstrap: this design was written by the orchestrator that dispatched the abandoned tasks. The reset records carry the operator's waiver form (`DESIGN_RESET_WAIVED_BY=operator`, decision 2026-10-11), this review is the only release, and no further orchestrator-authored design follows under T128; T127 (T120's redesign) is written by another context.
   220

+def parse_disposition(text: object) -> tuple[str | None, str] | None:
+    """Read `fixed:<commit>` as (commit, "") or `not-applicable:<reason>; evidence=<command>` as (None, reason)."""
+    if not isinstance(text, str):

+        return match.group("commit"), ""
+    body = text.removeprefix("not-applicable:")
+    # One split on the first delimiter and two linear checks; a second delimiter is refused.
+    if body == text or body.count(EVIDENCE_DELIMITER) != 1:
+        return None
+    reason, _, command = body.partition(EVIDENCE_DELIMITER)
+    return (None, reason.strip()) if reason.strip() and command.strip() else None

+def refuse_duplicate_keys(pairs: list[tuple[str, object]]) -> dict:
+    """json.loads keeps the last of two equal keys; the record's reader refuses them instead."""
+    seen: set[str] = set()
+    for key, _ in pairs:
+        if key in seen:
+            raise ValueError(f"acceptance record: duplicate key {key}")
+        seen.add(key)
+    return dict(pairs)
+

+def refuse_non_finite(name: str) -> object:
+    """json.loads accepts NaN and Infinity by default; a record field never needs one."""
+    raise ValueError("acceptance record: non-finite number")

+def read_acceptance_record(path: Path) -> tuple[dict | None, str | None]:
+    """Load the record's JSON block between its first two --- lines with the standard library only."""
+    # Both delimiters are whole lines that are exactly `---`: `---junk` closes nothing.
+    lines = path.read_text().split("\n")
+    if lines[0] != "---" or "---" not in lines[1:]:
+        return None, "acceptance record must start with a JSON block between two lines that are exactly ---"
+    block = "\n".join(lines[1 : lines.index("---", 1)])
+    try:
+        data = json.loads(block, object_pairs_hook=refuse_duplicate_keys, parse_constant=refuse_non_finite)
+    except json.JSONDecodeError as error:
+        return None, f"acceptance record: the block between the first two --- lines is not JSON: {error}"
+    except ValueError as error:
+        return None, str(error)
+    if not isinstance(data, dict):
+        return None, "acceptance record: the block must be one JSON object"
+    return data, None
+

+def swept_finding_ids(items: object, audit_summary: str | None, head: str) -> set[str]:
+    """The ids a ledger must cover: the sweep's Codex findings and the audit's numbered findings (a set, no regex)."""
+    ids: set[str] = set()
+    for item in items if isinstance(items, list) else []:
+        if not isinstance(item, dict) or item.get("author") != CODEX_BOT:
+            continue
+        url = item["url"] if isinstance(item.get("url"), str) else ""
+        body = item["body"] if isinstance(item.get("body"), str) else ""
+        if item.get("source") == "review_comment":
+            ids.add(url.rpartition("_r")[2])
+        elif item.get("source") == "review" and any(token in body for token in BADGE_TOKENS):
+            ids.add(url.rpartition("pullrequestreview-")[2])
+    if audit_summary is not None:
+        ids.update(f"audit:{head[:7]}:{n}" for n in range(1, len(AUDIT_FINDING.findall(audit_summary)) + 1))
+    return ids
+
+
+def audit_summary(root: Path) -> tuple[str | None, str | None]:
+    """The text of AUDIT_EVIDENCE's .last.md summary when AUDIT_EVIDENCE is set, which then requires it."""
+    value = os.environ.get(AUDIT_ENV, "").strip()
+    if not value:
+        return None, None
+    path = Path(value) if Path(value).is_absolute() else root / value
+    source = path.with_name(f"{path.name}.last.md")
+    if not source.is_file():
+        return (
+            None,
+            f"{AUDIT_ENV} verdict is missing: {source.name} must exist with codex's final message; re-run the audit",
+        )
+    return source.read_text(), None
+
+
+def acceptance_errors(
+    root: Path, required: bool, task: str | None, head: str, pr: object = None, items: object = None
+) -> tuple[list[str], dict | None]:
+    """The acceptance-record contract (plan 013 option A′): a JSON block bound to the task, HEAD and the swept PR."""
+    value = os.environ.get(ACCEPTANCE_ENV, "").strip()
+    if not value:
+        if required:
+            return [f"{ACCEPTANCE_ENV} must point to the task's acceptance record for PR integration"], None
+        return [], None
+    path = Path(value)
+    if not path.is_absolute():
+        path = root / path
+    path_error = orchestration_path_error(root, path, ACCEPTANCE_ENV, "acceptance")
+    if path_error:
+        return [path_error], None
+    # Bound like the audit: another task's record must not stand in for this one's.
+    if task is not None:
+        for name in (path.name, path.resolve().name):
+            if name != f"{task}.md":
+                return [
+                    f"{ACCEPTANCE_ENV} must be {task}.md, the record of the task named by {PR_FEEDBACK_ENV}, not {name}"
+                ], None
+    if not path.is_file():
+        return [f"{ACCEPTANCE_ENV} file does not exist: {path}"], None
+    record, error = read_acceptance_record(path)
+    if record is None:
+        return [f"{ACCEPTANCE_ENV} {error}"], None
+    errors = record_field_errors(record, path.name.removesuffix(".md"), head, pr)
+    if errors:
+        return errors, record
+    summary, summary_error = audit_summary(root)
+    if summary_error is not None:
+        return [summary_error], record
+    missing = swept_finding_ids(items, summary, head) - {str(row["id"]) for row in record["ledger"]}
+    if missing:
+        errors.append(f"S6: ledger lacks {', '.join(sorted(missing))}")
+    classes = Counter(row["class"] for row in record["ledger"])
+    stated = {entry["class"]: set(entry["records"]) for entry in record["searches"]}
+    for cls, count in classes.items():
+        if count < S6_CLASS_LIMIT:
+            continue
+        found = mistake_records(root, cls)
+        if isinstance(found, str):
+            errors.append(f"S6: class {cls} at {count}: {found}")
+        elif stated.get(cls) != found:
+            errors.append(f"S6: class {cls} at {count} without a matching records search")
+    return errors, record
+
+
+def mistake_records(root: Path, slug: str) -> set[str] | str:
+    """Recompute S6's records search with pathlib: the files with a `classes:` line naming the class.
+
+    The same match as `grep -rl 'classes:.*<class>'`, without a subprocess; the gate reads its result, never
+    pasted command text.
+    """
+    directory = root / MISTAKE_RECORDS
+    if not directory.is_dir():
+        return f"the records directory {MISTAKE_RECORDS} is missing"
+    found: set[str] = set()
+    for path in directory.rglob("*"):
+        if path.is_file() and not path.is_symlink():
+            lines = path.read_text(errors="replace").splitlines()
+            if any(line.startswith("classes:") and slug in line[len("classes:") :] for line in lines):
+                found.add(path.name)
+    return found
+

   343	def crit_data_errors(root: Path, source: str) -> list[str]:

    19	  It refuses a record whose ledger ids, as strings, do not include all of them, with `S6: ledger lacks <the missing ids, sorted>`. That is a set difference on exact strings: apart from the four badge tokens, no text of a body is read. The summary is required whenever `AUDIT_EVIDENCE` is set. A missing summary is refused with the text the audit check already uses (`… must exist with codex's final message`), because the coverage check runs before the audit check. Coverage is judged after the identity triple and the field checks, and before the S6 class count, so the class count reads a covered ledger.

{"id": "document:home/dot_config/claude/rules/crit-review.md", "summary": "Global Claude rule for the Crit agent-side self-review workflow: retrieving crit comment JSON as evidence, writing review receipts, and passing make require-crit-review before completion.", "filePath": "home/dot_config/claude/rules/crit-review.md"}
{"id": "document:home/dot_config/claude/rules/pr-integration.md", "summary": "Global Claude rule gating PR merges on a full GitHub feedback sweep via scripts/pr-feedback.py, per-item dispositions, and passing the evidence to make require-crit-review.", "filePath": "home/dot_config/claude/rules/pr-integration.md"}
{"id": "document:home/dot_agents/skills/gh-first-workflow/SKILL.md", "summary": "Agent skill enforcing gh-first GitHub issue/PR investigation, keeping PR descriptions in sync with the full PR, the pr-feedback.py disposition gate before merge, and Conventional Commit output.", "filePath": "home/dot_agents/skills/gh-first-workflow/SKILL.md"}
{"id": "document:home/dot_config/codex/AGENTS.md", "summary": "Global Codex instructions (Japanese): learn-index review at session start, one-line session summaries, worklog plan/todo rules, Crit agent-side review and PR-feedback integration gates, model profile selection from agent-config.yaml, Ponytail, Understand-Anything graph policy, and CompactionDB usage.", "filePath": "home/dot_config/codex/AGENTS.md"}
{"id": "file:scripts/pr-feedback.py", "summary": "Collector that gathers every piece of GitHub feedback on a PR head (issue comments, reviews, inline comments with thread state, non-passing checks, annotations, commit statuses) into one JSON document with empty dispositions for the PR integration gate.", "filePath": "scripts/pr-feedback.py"}
{"id": "function:scripts/pr-feedback.py:require_auth", "summary": "Exits with guidance when `gh auth status` reports the GitHub CLI is not authenticated.", "filePath": "scripts/pr-feedback.py"}
{"id": "function:scripts/pr-feedback.py:item", "summary": "Builds one normalized feedback item (source, actor, bot flag, level, body, url, path/line, thread state) with an empty disposition.", "filePath": "scripts/pr-feedback.py"}
{"id": "function:scripts/pr-feedback.py:thread_states", "summary": "Queries review threads over GraphQL and maps each review comment id to its resolved and outdated state.", "filePath": "scripts/pr-feedback.py"}
{"id": "function:scripts/pr-feedback.py:collect", "summary": "Fetches all PR feedback sources for the head commit via REST/GraphQL and assembles the item list with repo, PR, head and base metadata.", "filePath": "scripts/pr-feedback.py"}
{"id": "function:scripts/pr-feedback.py:main", "summary": "CLI entry that resolves the repo, requires gh auth, collects feedback, and writes JSON to stdout or a file.", "filePath": "scripts/pr-feedback.py"}
{"id": "file:scripts/require-crit-review.py", "summary": "Integration guard that requires native agent or Crit review evidence for meaningful diffs and, for PR integration, re-collects GitHub feedback from the authenticated base's pr-feedback.py and requires a root-cause disposition for every item.", "filePath": "scripts/require-crit-review.py"}
{"id": "function:scripts/require-crit-review.py:is_ignored", "summary": "Skips worklogs and the PR feedback evidence file itself when sizing a diff.", "filePath": "scripts/require-crit-review.py"}
{"id": "function:scripts/require-crit-review.py:feedback_path_error", "summary": "Rejects PR feedback evidence outside .orchestration/validation/ or without the -pr-feedback.json suffix.", "filePath": "scripts/require-crit-review.py"}
{"id": "function:scripts/require-crit-review.py:changed_paths", "summary": "Lists unstaged, staged, untracked, and optionally base...HEAD changed paths, excluding ignored files.", "filePath": "scripts/require-crit-review.py"}
{"id": "function:scripts/require-crit-review.py:numstat_line_count", "summary": "Sums added and removed line counts across working, staged, and base...HEAD diffs via git numstat.", "filePath": "scripts/require-crit-review.py"}
{"id": "function:scripts/require-crit-review.py:high_risk_reason", "summary": "Classifies a path as high risk (policy/config file, agent lifecycle prefix, or risky token) and returns the reason.", "filePath": "scripts/require-crit-review.py"}
{"id": "function:scripts/require-crit-review.py:review_reasons", "summary": "Aggregates reasons that make review mandatory: high-risk paths, many files, or large line counts.", "filePath": "scripts/require-crit-review.py"}
{"id": "function:scripts/require-crit-review.py:evidence_errors", "summary": "Validates the review receipt file and its required fields, dispatching to agent or Crit evidence checks.", "filePath": "scripts/require-crit-review.py"}
{"id": "function:scripts/require-crit-review.py:agent_review_errors", "summary": "Checks agent reviewer receipts require the crit-data surface, an allowed outcome, and valid Crit JSON evidence.", "filePath": "scripts/require-crit-review.py"}
{"id": "function:scripts/require-crit-review.py:crit_data_errors", "summary": "Validates repo-local Crit JSON evidence: inside the repo, a list of well-formed resolved records with at least one review/line/file scope.", "filePath": "scripts/require-crit-review.py"}
{"id": "function:scripts/require-crit-review.py:pr_feedback_errors", "summary": "Checks the filled pr-feedback JSON: correct head, valid fixed:<commit> or not-applicable:<reason> dispositions, failure reasons long enough, and fixed commits in range.", "filePath": "scripts/require-crit-review.py"}
{"id": "function:scripts/require-crit-review.py:pr_base_errors", "summary": "Binds the evidence's base to the PR's GitHub base and local repository before running any collector, rejecting stale or rewritten bases.", "filePath": "scripts/require-crit-review.py"}
{"id": "function:scripts/require-crit-review.py:collected_feedback_errors", "summary": "Re-runs the GitHub base's pr-feedback.py and requires every currently collected item to be present in the evidence.", "filePath": "scripts/require-crit-review.py"}
{"id": "function:scripts/require-crit-review.py:main", "summary": "CLI entry that decides whether review is required, validates base, review receipts, and PR feedback evidence, and exits non-zero on any error.", "filePath": "scripts/require-crit-review.py"}
{"id": "file:tests/unit/test_pr_feedback.py", "summary": "unittest suite running pr-feedback.py against recorded GitHub REST/GraphQL responses (no network), plus parity checks that the PR integration rule, its symlink, and skills carry the same requirements.", "filePath": "tests/unit/test_pr_feedback.py"}
{"id": "function:tests/unit/test_pr_feedback.py:load_script", "summary": "Imports scripts/pr-feedback.py as a module for testing against recorded responses.", "filePath": "tests/unit/test_pr_feedback.py"}
{"id": "file:tests/unit/test_require_crit_review.py", "summary": "Large unittest suite for require-crit-review.py in isolated git repositories: when review is required, crit/agent evidence validation, base binding to the GitHub PR base, and PR feedback evidence dispositions.", "filePath": "tests/unit/test_require_crit_review.py"}

20 {"source": "review_comment", "author": "chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]", "bot": true, "level": "comment", "path": "scripts/require-crit-review.py", "line": 769, "body": "**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Validate list-prefixed audit findings**\n\nWhen an acceptance record formats a disposition as a Markdown list item, for example `- audit-finding: 1 … not-applicable:<reason>`, `str.strip()` leaves the `- ` prefix and this `startswith` check skips it. This is an existing record format (for example `.orchestration/acceptance/dotfiles-T65-agent-stop-gate-a01.md:41`), so with a `correct` audit verdict the merge gate accepts such a line without the newly required `evidence=` clause. Strip an optional Markdown list marker or match the disposition prefix explicitly; the closed acceptance-input threat-table test currently exercises only unprefixed lines.\n\nAGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L77-L78](https://github.com/mryfmo/dotfiles/blob/386a71b3bf3992488ca3942c2390dfe7160d1f69/AGENTS.md#L77-L78)\n\nUseful? 21 {"source": "review_comment", "author": "chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]", "bot": true, "level": "comment", "path": "scripts/require-crit-review.py", "line": 29, "body": "**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject repeated evidence delimiters**\n\nWhen a disposition contains multiple `; evidence=` delimiters, the greedy reason group splits at the last one. Consequently `not-applicable:; evidence=echo proof; evidence=true` is accepted with `; evidence=echo proof` as its supposedly non-empty reason, and a failure-level item can similarly pad a one-character reason past the 20-character minimum. This bypass affects PR feedback, audit dispositions, and acceptance-record validation through the shared regex; parse the first delimiter or explicitly reject additional delimiters. The closed acceptance-input threat-table test does not exercise this case.\n\nAGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L77-L78](https://github.com/mryfmo/dotfiles/blob/d5d6c9b1b22c32e483f76ed2d313571a487aa16a/AGENTS.md#L77-L78)\n\nUseful? React with 👍 / 👎.", "url": "https://github.com/mryfmo/dotfiles/pull/329#discussion_r4248934816", "resolved": false, "outdated": true, "disposition": "fixed:c6cf0548"}

   479	def feedback_key(item: dict, masked: bool = False) -> tuple:
   480	    """Identify a feedback item; `masked` takes its body and path as `--mask-secrets` saves them.
   481	
   482	    A saved body or path may be verbatim or exactly that masked form, because
   483	    masking (`validate-agent-assets.py --mask-secrets`, which masks the string
   484	    values of a JSON file) is the repository's documented way to keep evidence
   485	    scannable, and the url still identifies the item. Source, url, level, line
   486	    and author stay byte-exact; the author decides which items the acceptance
   487	    record's ledger must cover, so it is matched against the live collection too.
   488	    """
   489	    key = {field: item.get(field) for field in ("source", "url", "level", "path", "line", "body", "author")}
   490	    if masked:
   491	        # Only the body and a key-shaped file path may be masked; the rest is exact.
   492	        for field in ("path", "body"):
   493	            if isinstance(key[field], str):
   494	                key[field] = validator().mask_secret_matches(key[field])[0]
   495	    return tuple(key.values())

   498	def missing_feedback(collected: list, saved: list) -> Counter:
   499	    """Count collected items with no saved item, verbatim or masked, left to match."""
   500	    available = Counter(feedback_key(item) for item in saved if isinstance(item, dict))
   501	    missing: Counter = Counter()
   502	    for item in collected:
   503	        for key in dict.fromkeys((feedback_key(item), feedback_key(item, masked=True))):
   504	            if available[key]:
   505	                available[key] -= 1
   506	                break
   507	        else:
   508	            missing[feedback_key(item)] += 1
   509	    return missing

   584	def collected_feedback_errors(root: Path, evidence: dict, head: str, base: str) -> list[str]:
   585	    """Re-collect the PR's feedback and require every current item in the evidence.
   586	
   587	    A hand-written or stale document cannot pass: the guard runs the GitHub
   588	    base SHA's scripts/pr-feedback.py (the PR under review cannot swap it) for the
   589	    evidence's PR, requires the PR head on GitHub to be this HEAD, and requires
   590	    each collected item (as a multiset) to be present. A bot review is not
   591	    required; when one exists it is collected and must be dispositioned like any
   592	    other item.
   593	    """
   594	    pr = evidence.get("pr")
   595	    if not isinstance(pr, int) or isinstance(pr, bool) or pr <= 0:
   596	        return [f"{PR_FEEDBACK_ENV} must name its pull request number in `pr`"]
   597	    errors = pr_base_errors(root, evidence, pr, head, base)
   598	    if errors:
   599	        return errors
   600	    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as temporary:
   601	        collected_path = Path(temporary) / "collected.json"
   602	        # An advanced local base may contain untrusted code despite a safe merge-base.
   603	        # Execute only the GitHub-authenticated base's collector, including bootstrap.
   604	        collector = root / "scripts/pr-feedback.py"
   605	        base_collector = run_git(["show", f"{evidence['base_sha']}:scripts/pr-feedback.py"], root)
   606	        if base_collector.returncode == 0:
   607	            collector = Path(temporary) / "pr-feedback.py"
   608	            collector.write_text(base_collector.stdout)
   609	        result = subprocess.run(
   610	            [sys.executable, str(collector), str(pr), "--repo", evidence["repo"], "--json", str(collected_path)],
   611	            cwd=root,
   612	            check=False,
   613	            text=True,
   614	            stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
   615	            stderr=subprocess.PIPE,
   616	        )
   617	        if result.returncode != 0 or not collected_path.is_file():
   618	            detail = (result.stderr or result.stdout).strip().splitlines()[-1:] or ["no output"]
   619	            return [f"could not re-collect PR #{pr} feedback with scripts/pr-feedback.py: {detail[0]}"]
   620	        collected = json.loads(collected_path.read_text())
   621	    if collected.get("head_sha") != head:
   622	        return [f"PR #{pr} head on GitHub is {collected.get('head_sha')}, not the local HEAD {head}; push first"]
   623	    if collected.get("repo") != evidence["repo"]:
   624	        return [f"collected feedback does not match the local GitHub repository {evidence['repo']}"]
   625	    missing = missing_feedback(collected.get("items", []), evidence.get("items", []))

+    def test_s6_searches_entry_must_equal_the_recomputed_records_search(self) -> None:
+        # The search finds the base's M-20261012-3.md (classes: [evidence, class-count-scope]); only a line that
+        # begins with `classes:` counts, so M-20261012-9.md, which names `scope` elsewhere, is not found.
+        run(["git", "branch", "-M", "main"], self.temp_dir)
+        feedback = self.write_feedback([])
+        self.write_review_file(
+            ".orchestration/learning/mistakes/M-20261012-9.md", "---\nartifact: a scope review\nclasses: [other]\n---\n"
+        )
+
+        def ledger(cls: str) -> list[dict]:
+            return [{"id": f"42441288{index:02d}", "class": cls} for index in range(2)] + [
+                {"id": "audit:3a54d34:1", "class": cls}
+            ]
+
+        refused = "S6: class scope at 3 without a matching records search"
+        for label, fields, message in (
+            (
+                "the matching set",
+                {"ledger": ledger("scope"), "searches": [{"class": "scope", "records": ["M-20261012-3.md"]}]},
+                None,
+            ),
+            (
+                "none where nothing matches",
+                {"ledger": ledger("absent"), "searches": [{"class": "absent", "records": []}]},
+                None,
+            ),
+            ("a record missing", {"ledger": ledger("scope"), "searches": [{"class": "scope", "records": []}]}, refused),
+            (
+                "a record too many",
+                {"ledger": ledger("scope"), "searches": [{"class": "scope", "records": ["M-20261012-3.md", "M-9.md"]}]},
+                refused,
+            ),
+            (
+                "another class's entry",
+                {
+                    "ledger": ledger("scope"),
+                    "searches": [{"class": "class-count-scope", "records": ["M-20261012-3.md"]}],
+                },
+                refused,
+            ),
+            (
+                "a pasted command for its records",
+                {
+                    "ledger": ledger("scope"),
+                    "searches": [{"class": "scope", "records": ["grep -rl 'classes:.*scope' ."]}],
+                },
+                refused,
+            ),
+        ):
+            with self.subTest(label):
+                record = self.write_record(**fields)
+                result = self.guard_base({"PR_FEEDBACK_EVIDENCE": feedback, "ACCEPTANCE_EVIDENCE": record})
+                if message is None:
+                    self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 0, result.stdout)
+                else:
+                    self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 1, result.stdout)
+                    self.assertIn(message, result.stdout)
+        shutil.rmtree(self.temp_dir / ".orchestration/learning/mistakes")
+        record = self.write_record(ledger=ledger("scope"), searches=[{"class": "scope", "records": []}])
+        result = self.guard_base({"PR_FEEDBACK_EVIDENCE": feedback, "ACCEPTANCE_EVIDENCE": record})
+        self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 1, result.stdout)
+        self.assertIn(
+            "S6: class scope at 3: the records directory .orchestration/learning/mistakes/ is missing", result.stdout
+        )
+
+    def test_base_requires_an_acceptance_record_under_acceptance(self) -> None:
+        # The threat row for the ACCEPTANCE_EVIDENCE input: its path, then each front-matter field.
+        run(["git", "branch", "-M", "main"], self.temp_dir)

+        other = self.write_review_file(".orchestration/acceptance/other.md", "# another task's record\n")
+        (self.temp_dir / ".orchestration/acceptance/alias.md").symlink_to(other)
+        own = ".orchestration/acceptance/test.md"
+        for value, message in (
+            ("", "ACCEPTANCE_EVIDENCE must point to the task's acceptance record for PR integration"),
+            (".orchestration/validation/test.md", "ACCEPTANCE_EVIDENCE must live under .orchestration/acceptance/"),
+            (".orchestration/acceptance/other.md", "must be test.md, the record of the task named by"),

+                result = self.guard_base({"PR_FEEDBACK_EVIDENCE": feedback, "ACCEPTANCE_EVIDENCE": value})
+                self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 1, result.stdout)
+                self.assertIn(message, result.stdout)
+        for label, write, message in (
+            (
+                "no block",

+                "acceptance record must start with a JSON block between two lines that are exactly ---",
+            ),
+            (
+                "a closing line that is not exactly ---",
+                {"text": '---\n{"format": 1}\n---junk\n'},
+                "acceptance record must start with a JSON block between two lines that are exactly ---",
+            ),
+            (
+                "not JSON",
+                {"text": "---\nformat: 1\n---\n"},
+                "acceptance record: the block between the first two --- lines is not JSON",
+            ),
+            (
+                "a list, not an object",
+                {"text": "---\n[1]\n---\n"},
+                "acceptance record: the block must be one JSON object",
+            ),
+            ("a non-finite number", {"fixture": "acceptance-nan.md"}, "acceptance record: non-finite number"),
+            ("a duplicate key", {"fixture": "acceptance-duplicate-key.md"}, "acceptance record: duplicate key ledger"),
+            ("format", {"format": 2}, "format must be 1"),

+            (
+                "head",
+                {"fixture": "acceptance-stale-head.md"},
+                "acceptance record head 0000000000000000000000000000000000000000 is not HEAD",

+            ("pr of another PR", {"fixture": "acceptance-wrong-pr.md"}, "acceptance record pr 2 is not the swept pr 1"),
+            ("ledger id", {"ledger": [{"id": "123", "class": "scope"}]}, "ledger row 0 must be"),
+            ("ledger class", {"ledger": [{"id": 4244128846, "class": "Scope;x"}]}, "ledger row 0 must be"),
+            ("searches records", {"searches": [{"class": "scope", "records": "M-1.md"}]}, "searches entry 0 must be"),
+            (
+                "searches twice for one class",
+                {"searches": [{"class": "scope", "records": []}, {"class": "scope", "records": []}]},
+                "searches names class scope more than once",
+            ),
+            ("audit_findings entry", {"audit_findings": [{"n": "1", "fixed": "abcdef0"}]}, "a fix moves HEAD"),
+            (
+                "S6",
+                {"fixture": "acceptance-s6-missing.md"},
+                "S6: class class-count-scope at 3 without a matching records search",

+                result = self.guard_base({"PR_FEEDBACK_EVIDENCE": feedback, "ACCEPTANCE_EVIDENCE": record})

+    def test_disposition_parsing_is_linear(self) -> None:
+        # Thread 4249544794: one split and two checks, so a long malformed disposition is refused at once.
+        spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("require_crit_review", GUARD)
+        guard = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
+        spec.loader.exec_module(guard)
+        for text in (
+            "not-applicable:" + "a" * 1_000_000,
+            "not-applicable:" + "a" * 1_000_000 + "; evidence=b; evidence=c",
+        ):
+            started = time.perf_counter()
+            self.assertIsNone(guard.parse_disposition(text))

threat_model:
  R1: rounds are judged by models re-reading models and add no deterministic fact, so a wrong premise is patched round after round (T118 20 revises, T119 5 revises and 4 audits; the vendor's own rule is two corrections, then start fresh)
  R2: "hand-written parsers at a trust boundary have an unbounded bypass surface (PR 313: 33 of 52 Bot threads on a 503-line validator with its own YAML parser, written on the false premise that PyYAML is unavailable)"
  R3: "PRs larger than a reviewer can hold (PR 313 20 files +2642, PR 312 37 files +3191; Google: 100 lines reasonable, 1000 too large)"
  R4: task text grown by question-and-amendment (PR 313 6 questions 8 amendments, T119 8 and 8, T120 8 amendments and no RESULT) keeps the under-researched premise
  R5: the orchestrator's artifacts are unaudited and it dispositions findings about itself (T119 audit-finding 2); the reset rule was prose the orchestrator could waive (PR 313 revise round 2)
  R6: "the auditor becomes a serial queue when audits run once per round in one tab (measured: 4 audits about 1.3 h of T119's 11.1 h; the rounds, not the audits, were the cost)"
  R7: cost is unmeasured (every acceptance record says cost n/a) so no stage can be weighed against its value
  R8: a PR can change the check that judges it (a pull_request workflow runs the PR head's workflow file); host-side evidence is whatever the orchestrator copies into the gate's cwd

  - mechanical checks run from main's workflow file as a pull_request_target required status check that reads PR files as data and executes nothing from the PR; required workflows are organization-only, so this is the main-pinned form available to a user-owned repository
  - the operator waiver is visible, not prevented (acceptance record, boundary PR body, check-regime-boundary)
  - a reset is released only by a redesign written in a context other than the one that wrote the abandoned task, or by the operator

# AGMSG-TASK dotfiles-T128-regime-v3-a01 — DESIGN: regime v3, the redesign after the 2026-10-10 halt

Drafted 2026-10-11 (local) by the orchestrator seat `claude-deep-dot` under a recorded bootstrap exception (operator decision 2026-10-11: the orchestrator drafts, a fresh context on the review profile must accept before any implementing task is dispatched). Operator direction (pasted 2026-10-11): when substantive findings repeat, the design, implementation or verification is wrong and a mechanism must force the redo; prose alone repeats the mistake; the auditor must be able to find the orchestrator's and the worker's mistakes; efficiency, quality and cost are optimised together; the auditor must not become the bottleneck and the audit stages must be chosen; all of it grounded in the tools' official documentation and current practice. Research inputs: fact sheets on Claude Code 2.1.293, Codex CLI 0.161.0, GitHub rulesets and Actions, and the research literature, read 2026-10-11; the measured baseline below.

## 1. Finding: the fix program tripped its own rule

By T126 INV-6 as written: wave 1 (PR #313) 8 amendments (limit 4) and 2 revises (limit 2); wave 3b (PR #314) Bot P1 on two post-RESULT heads. The orchestrator was drafting a waiver for #313. T120 was reset only on the operator's question. The regime is therefore reset here by its own rule; this document is the redesign, and T126 and T124 are superseded (their accepted ideas are kept where named).

Measured baseline (history + GitHub):

| task | PR | files | +lines | amendments | questions | revises | audits (incorrect) | Bot threads (heads) | P0/P1 | wall |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| T114 | - | - | - | 0 | 0 | 6 | 3 (3) | - | - | 21.5h |
| T118 | 310 | 35 | 881 | 7 | 0 | 20 | 8 (7) | 16 (7) | 0 | 10.6h |
| T119 | 312 | 37 | 3191 | 8 | 8 | 5 | 4 (4) | 25 (11) | 7 | 11.1h |
| T120 | 315 | 19 | 1489 | 8 | 1 | 0 | 0 | 15 (5) | 8 | reset |
| T124 W1 | 313 | 20 | 2642 | 8 | 6 | 2 | 0 | 52 (10) | 31 | halted, reset |
| T124 W3b | 314 | 9 | 1462 | 5 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 24 (4) | 2 | halted, reset |

Every acceptance record to date says `cost: n/a`.

## 2. Root causes, each with its evidence

R1 to R8 in the front matter. The literature behind R1: intrinsic self-correction without an external signal degrades after the first round (Huang et al. 2023); a second review round on the same artifact raised recall slightly and false positives by 62% (arXiv 2603.16244); multi-round review degrades with rounds (MCR-Bench); revising an already-correct state loses correct work unless verifier evidence is bound to the exact code state (arXiv 2607.24604). Behind R3: Google's review study (median change 24 lines, ~90% under 10 files) and its CL-size guidance. Behind R5 and R6: a judge without a reference is lenient and a reference flips 9-85% of verdicts toward correct (2607.12885); format-restricted generation degrades reasoning, so verdicts reason first and then fill the schema (2408.02442); Anthropic's harness-design post: a standalone skeptical evaluator is tractable where a self-critical generator is not, and the evaluator is worth its cost only where the task exceeds the model's reliable solo capability, which is what the tier table encodes.

## 3. Principles (each names what it reuses and what it deletes)

- **P1 One deterministic fact per round (INV-3).** Reuses tests/unit, CI, `pr-feedback.py`. Deletes free-form revise rounds and the audit-per-round habit.
- **P2 Declarative over imperative at trust boundaries (INV-1, INV-5, INV-7).** Reuses `jsonschema`, PyYAML, `codex exec --output-schema`, `claude -p --json-schema`. Deletes the bespoke YAML parser, the glob NFA, the prose verdict grammar, regex parsing of `.last.md`, and the T126 "process_tiers.json next to the module" indirection (the validator reads the manifest with PyYAML).
- **P3 Small one-invariant PRs enforced in CI (INV-2).** Reuses GitHub required checks and the strict up-to-date ruleset already in force. Deletes waves declared inside a task file.
- **P4 Main-pinned mechanical checks in CI; host gate only for history-anchored rules (INV-1, INV-2, INV-8 in CI; INV-3, INV-5 record, INV-6, INV-7 anchor, INV-11 on the host).** Reuses `pull_request_target`, the `changes` job pattern that reports success for an `.orchestration`-only diff. Deletes PR #313's `REVIEW_TREE` idea (never on `main`) and the copy step of untracked evidence into the gate's cwd. The host gate `make require-crit-review` keeps its evidence rules and changes three of them in named waves: the audit verdict and categories come from the schema JSON with the `AGMSG-AUDIT` record and the category lock (V2b), the reset backstop and the Bot-head count (V3a), the history-anchored design review (V4); it continues to run from the orchestrator's main checkout.
- **P5 Research before dispatch; a question ends the task, not amends it (INV-4).** Reuses history (`amendment=`, `status=question`). Deletes the amendment-per-question practice. The task file's `premises` block is the mechanical residue of "verify every CLI constraint by running the real command".
- **P6 Reset is mechanical, loop-time, and released only by another context or the operator (INV-6).** Reuses `scripts/require-crit-review.py` as the mandatory point, `agent-stop-gate.sh` and the Codex `[hooks].Stop` as the early signal (both soft by their documented caps: Claude's 8-continuation cap, Codex's continuation prompt), `check-regime-boundary.sh` for the re-dispatch detector. Deletes the orchestrator-written redesign (the redesign author is a `review`-profile seat or a fresh headless context; the `redesign` profile of T124 v4 is dropped: `review` is the same model and effort as `deep`, so independence of context is the whole lever, and T124 round 1 showed it works).
- **P7 Audit staging by tier; the auditor never serializes the pipeline (INV-5, process_tiers).** See section 4.
- **P8 Cost measured, budgets per tier (INV-9).** Reuses the JSON cost fields the runtimes already emit and the session transcripts. Deletes `cost: n/a`.
- **P9 Parallelism with disjoint files and early push (INV-10).** Reuses `herdr-agents --add-worker`, draft PRs.
- **P10 Routing stays by boundary.** Claude-boundary sources to a Codex seat, Codex-boundary to a Claude seat, permgate and shared gate sources to the operator, as the agmsg-orchestration skill's step 3 states; nothing here changes that.

## 4. Audit stages (process_tiers; the one table the validator reads)

| stage | who | when | tier docs | tier review | tier design | cost |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 design review | a fresh Claude context on the review profile and a Codex read-only review of the same hash, schema receipts (INV-7) | before any code | - | - | required | minutes |
| 1 worker checks | worker in its sandbox: invariant tests first, shellcheck, unit tests | before every push | required | required | required | none for the regime |
| 2 CI + Bot | main-pinned `regime` check (schema, caps, evidence shape) + unit tests + Codex Bot | every push, in parallel | required | required | required | none |
| 3 schema audit | headless read-only `codex exec --output-schema`, pooled 2, started by `make audit-head` once CI is green and the Bot reviewed or 15 min passed, once per RESULT head, reused for an evidence-only head by tree equality (INV-5) | per RESULT head | - | required | required, with invariant map and permgate window | the scarce resource, now off the critical path |
| 4 acceptance | orchestrator: sweep, dispositions, record, host gate, merge `--match-head-commit` | per RESULT | required | required | required | minutes |

Tier derivation: docs = prose-only `allowed_files` outside the regime's own rule prose (`home/dot_config/claude/rules/**`, the agmsg-orchestration SKILL, `AGENTS.md`, README), which is review tier by explicit list; review = the existing review-tier paths (scripts, hooks, tests, templates); design = the explicit design-tier list from T124 INV-2 v3 (install/**, setup.sh, the gate scripts, `executable_herdr-agents`, `executable_permgate`, Codex and Claude policy, sandbox and permission settings, credential helpers). Round limits: docs 1 revise; review and design 2 revises then reset. Profiles: worker `standard` (docs `express`), review `review`, audit `audit`.

Why stage 3 is not the queue: the orchestrator starts it with `make audit-head` when the RESULT arrives (the wait on CI and the Bot is inside the target), it runs concurrently (pool of two, each in its own detached worktree), once per head, and an evidence-only head reuses the earlier audit by tree equality; the measured cost of the old serial form was 1.3 h of 11.1 h, so the throughput levers are P1 and P6, and the pool removes the residual queue.

Edits, the unit tests, ruff, prettier, the mutation checks, the records-only `make require-crit-review` and the commits ran inside the sandbox. No `allowed_domains`.
- Worktree `.claude/worktrees/worker-f`, branch `regime/gate-evidence` (created for a01 with `git switch -c regime/gate-evidence --no-track origin/main`, so `.git/config` gained no upstream). Commits use `git -c commit.gpgsign=false`.
- Two sandbox effects on test runs, both environment-only:
  - The global `commit.gpgsign` reads `~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub`, which the sandbox denies, so every `git commit` inside the test fixtures fails and the module showed 73 failures on unmodified `origin/main`. Test runs set `GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=1 GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0=commit.gpgsign GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0=false` for their own process (validation §2).
  - PyPI is unreachable; `--with pyyaml` runs use `UV_OFFLINE=1`.
  - Under the YAML form (`b2b3db45` to `7581d590`), the gate spawned `uv run --offline … --with pyyaml` for the acceptance record. Overnight the uv cache was pruned to 38M, without PyYAML: every offline load then failed, the online retry was blocked (pypi.org is not in the sandbox allowlist), and a module run timed out at 600 s. One command with `allowed_domains` pypi.org and files.pythonhosted.org fetched PyYAML 6.0.3 back. Amendment 1 (plan 013 A′) removed the subprocess: the gate now reads a JSON block with the standard library, so the gate makes no network call.
- The full unit suite fails the same 78 tests on this branch as on `origin/main`, in six modules no file of this task feeds (validation §7).
- Scratch worktrees of `origin/main` and of the code heads (`$TMPDIR/basewt`, `recwt` to `recwt10`, all detached) served the base comparisons and the records-only runs, and were removed with `git worktree remove` (`--force` only for an untracked probe file).
- The first push, `git push origin regime/gate-evidence`, failed ("Could not read from remote repository"), because the global `url.git@github.com:.pushinsteadof` turns the HTTPS remote into SSH, and there is no SSH key. Every push since uses `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null git -c credential.helper= -c 'credential.helper=!gh auth git-credential' push https://github.com/mryfmo/dotfiles regime/gate-evidence`.
- Out-of-sandbox actions are only the Worker Playbook step 4 cases: `git push`, `gh`, the main-checkout CompactionDB `memory add`, writing and masking the main-checkout evidence copies, and `agmsg-dispatch` (`excludedCommands`). The main-checkout copy of this file counts them.
- Revise 1 (audit finding 2): call 7 of the main-checkout copy ran a local branch creation, a checkout and the commit `27e8a0ea` outside the sandbox, chained after a fetch. From the revise on, every repository mutation runs inside the sandbox. That covers the fetch of `20d776d4`, `git switch`, the `--ff-only` merge, both commits (`2231a4f7`, `09caaa91`), the scratch worktree `$TMPDIR/revwt` and both HTTPS pushes. Only the `gh` reads (Bot wait, CI, reviews) run outside it, because `gh` fails TLS verification in the sandbox (`x509: OSStatus -26276`).

916     summary, summary_error = audit_summary(root)
917     if summary_error is not None:
918         return [summary_error], record
919     missing = swept_finding_ids(items, summary, head) - {str(row["id"]) for row in record["ledger"]}
920     if missing:
921         errors.append(f"S6: ledger lacks {', '.join(sorted(missing))}")
922     classes = Counter(row["class"] for row in record["ledger"])
923     stated = {entry["class"]: set(entry["records"]) for entry in record["searches"]}
924     for cls, count in classes.items():
925         if count < S6_CLASS_LIMIT:
926             continue
927         found = mistake_records(root, cls)
928         if isinstance(found, str):
929             errors.append(f"S6: class {cls} at {count}: {found}")
930         elif stated.get(cls) != found:
931             errors.append(f"S6: class {cls} at {count} without a matching records search")
932     return errors, record
933 
934 
935 def mistake_records(root: Path, slug: str) -> set[str] | str:
936     """Recompute S6's records search with pathlib: the files with a `classes:` line naming the class.
937 
938     The same match as `grep -rl 'classes:.*<class>'`, without a subprocess; the gate reads its result, never
939     pasted command text.
940     """
941     directory = root / MISTAKE_RECORDS
942     if not directory.is_dir():
943         return f"the records directory {MISTAKE_RECORDS} is missing"
944     found: set[str] = set()
945     for path in directory.rglob("*"):
946         if path.is_file() and not path.is_symlink():
947             lines = path.read_text(errors="replace").splitlines()
948             if any(line.startswith("classes:") and slug in line[len("classes:") :] for line in lines):
949                 found.add(path.name)
950     return found
951 
952 
953 def evidence_field(text: str, field: str) -> str | None:
954     prefix = f"{field}:"
955     for line in text.splitlines():
956         if line.startswith(prefix):
957             return line[len(prefix) :].strip()
